brief.headline: Ask for ₹205/kg on laminates — the bottom of the fair market band — and offer to pay in 15 days to free up ₹320 cash for us.

priceAsk.summary: Push laminate price to ₹205/kg, the low end of the market fair band.
priceAsk.basis: Market asking prices for pharma/ORS sachet laminate sit in a ₹205–305/kg band, with ₹250/kg typical. We should anchor at the bottom of that fair range — ₹205/kg — because we have two proven alternate converters (Huhtamaki and UFLEX) already on our books who can handle this volume, plus a strong converter lead (Constantia Parikh) to qualify.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to cut payment days from 30 to 15 in return for hitting the ₹205/kg target.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹320 cash for us, so we trade that liquidity for a solid price lock.

brief.financialLeverage: Silk Polypack publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or cash position. That means we lean on what we do know: our ₹7775 annual spend is tiny — unlikely to give us much weight — but we have real, credible alternates already supplying FDC (Huhtamaki and UFLEX are both listed converters). The plan is to qualify a second source now and use that competition to hold the line at ₹205/kg. If they won't move, we split volume or switch.

evidence.point: Market asking price for pharma/ORS sachet laminate runs ₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg, and the verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR (top of fair band)'.
BOPET film import value — the raw substrate — is ₹171.60/kg, giving us a rough floor for the material cost inside the laminate.
Our annual spend with Silk Polypack is ₹7775 — a very small account, so our leverage is low on volume alone.
We currently pay 30 days after receipt; moving to 15 days frees up ₹320 cash for us.
Huhtamaki India (₹2758.00 Cr revenue, listed, health 59/100) is already a tiny FDC supplier and a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets.
UFLEX (₹16492.00 Cr revenue, listed, health 46/100) is a flexibles giant doing both film and conversion — another credible second source at scale.

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already a tiny FDC supplier, revenue ₹2758.00 Cr, health 59/100 — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant (₹16492.00 Cr revenue, health 46/100) that makes both film substrate and does conversion — can second-source laminates at scale.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, does pharma blister and sachet laminates (₹222.04 Cr revenue, health 31/100) — a strong second-source lead to qualify before the next RFQ.

risks: Our ₹7775 annual spend is tiny, so Silk Polypack has little incentive to cut price for volume — we must lead with the credible threat of a second source.

Silk Polypack's financials aren't public, so we can't see if they're cash-tight or healthy — watch for signs of stress (late deliveries, quality slips) that might mean they need our business more than they let on.
If we push too hard on price without a qualified backup, they may walk or short us — make sure Huhtamaki or Constantia Parikh is RFQ-ready before the final ask.

Switching to a new converter mid-year risks a qualification delay and possible stock-out — phase any move carefully, and keep Silk Polypack in the loop that we're qualifying alternates (it's normal due diligence, not a threat).
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in ₹205/kg — the low end of the fair market band for pharma laminate — and in return we'll cut our payment cycle to 15 days, freeing up cash for both of us.
